classification.difficultyReason: Choose positive-denominator multiplication and case analysis, solve a quadratic with irrational roots and reject intervals outside their case.

answer.worked:
The domain requires $x\ne4$. Since $|x-4|>0$, multiplication preserves the inequality:
$$(3-x)|x-4|>1.$$
For $x>4$:
$$\begin{aligned}(3-x)(x-4)&>1\\-x^2+7x-12&>1\\-x^2+7x-13&>0\end{aligned}$$
Here $\Delta=49-52=-3<0$. The quadratic has a negative leading coefficient and is always negative, so this case has no solution.

For $x<4$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(3-x)(x-4)&>1\\x^2-7x+12&>1\\x^2-7x+11&>0\end{aligned}$$
The roots are $\dfrac{7-\sqrt5}{2}$ and $\dfrac{7+\sqrt5}{2}$. Hence
$$x<\frac{7-\sqrt5}{2}\quad\text{or}\quad x>\frac{7+\sqrt5}{2}.$$
Restricting to $x<4$ leaves
$$x<\frac{7-\sqrt5}{2}.$$
